c3_dialog.text: Install Core Mail Review the server-resolved plan before starting. Nothing changes until you confirm. Component and packages Version Postfix postfix 3.10.13 Dovecot dovecot-imapd, dovecot-pop3d, dovecot-lmtpd 2.4.1 Service impact These services may restart or reload: Postfix, Dovecot. Firewall impact The profile requires these inbound ports: 110/tcp, 143/tcp, 25/tcp, 465/tcp, 587/tcp, 993/tcp, 995/tcp. On this server mail is added through server setup, so it gets the same steps and checks as setup: the public DNS record of the mail host name, a trusted certificate and its renewal, reverse DNS (PTR) and outgoing port 25. You review the changes there before anything starts. Mail hostname System hostname: dns-debian13. Choose the address for mail services and their certificate; this does not rename the server. Name the mail server answers as Mail services will use panel.set18.test. The system hostname is preserved. Suggested from the certificate this panel is reached at. Cancel Review in server setup

mail_dns_wait_seen.guidance: Verify public DNS before certificate issuance: mail.set18.test Certificate issuance requires this public A record: mail.set18.test → 192.0.2.10. The public record has not been verified yet. This result alone does not establish whether the record is absent or a DNS server is unreachable. Create or correct this record at the DNS provider or primary that manages it. You do not need to create a website in Domains. This prerequisite is checked automatically. After it passes, the same setup continues. To change the reviewed names or addresses, use Edit plan below. Edit plan Checks and how to continue

page_lines.text: The public resolver 1.1.1.1 reports host-192-0-2-10.provider.set18.test as the reverse DNS (PTR) name of this server’s address 192.0.2.10; mail servers expect mail.set18.test. You set this at your server provider, not in CelikPanel: in the provider’s control panel, or by asking its support to set the reverse DNS of 192.0.2.10 to mail.set18.test.
